opts: Diabetic client, glucose 52, sweaty and shaky
first.why: Glucose 52 with symptoms is unstable right now. Treat with 15 g fast-acting carbs and recheck in 15 minutes.
New chest pain after an MI could be another infarction. Assess, get a 12-lead ECG and notify the provider.
Stridor after thyroid surgery signals airway swelling or hematoma. Airway always comes first.

opts: New leg cast, toes cool, pale and numb
first.why: Cool, pale, numb toes under a cast point to impaired circulation or compartment syndrome. Act fast to save the limb.

opts: Receiving blood, new back pain and chills
first.why: Back pain and chills during a transfusion suggest a reaction. Stop the blood and keep the line open with saline.
Bradycardia plus nausea in a client on digoxin are classic toxicity signs. Hold the dose and check a level.
Drooling and tripod positioning suggest epiglottitis, an airway emergency. Don't examine the throat.
Severe-range BP with a headache points to severe preeclampsia and seizure risk.

opts: One swollen calf, now sudden dyspnea
Asthma, peak flow in the green zone
first.why: A swollen calf followed by sudden shortness of breath suggests a DVT that became a PE.

opts: Face burns, singed nose hair, hoarse voice
first.why: Singed nasal hair and hoarseness signal inhalation injury. The airway can swell shut quickly.

opts: Back pain, wants a heat pack
first.why: A falling GCS means rising intracranial pressure until proven otherwise. A change in LOC is an early warning sign.

opts: DKA on insulin drip, K 3.1 mEq/L
first.why: Insulin drives potassium into cells. A K of 3.1 on a drip risks dangerous arrhythmias.

opts: Post-op, wound open with organs visible
first.why: Evisceration is an emergency. Cover with sterile saline-moist dressing, stay with the client and call for help.

opts: Voices telling them to hurt others
first.why: Command hallucinations to harm others are a safety risk for everyone on the unit. Safety comes first.
RR under 12 and absent reflexes signal magnesium toxicity. Stop the infusion; calcium gluconate is the antidote.
Wheezing after a new antibiotic suggests anaphylaxis. Stop the drug and prepare epinephrine.
Groin swelling after a cath may be bleeding or a hematoma. Apply pressure and assess right away.

quiz.why: K is 3.5 to 5.0. 135 to 145 is sodium, a common trap.
Low pH with high CO2. Respiratory problems move pH and CO2 in opposite directions.
Protamine reverses heparin. Vitamin K reverses warfarin.
Vitamin K reverses warfarin. Monitor PT and INR.
Most indications target 2 to 3. 0.8 to 1.1 is normal without anticoagulation.

quiz.q: Ordered 500 mg. Supply is 250 mg per 5 mL. How many mL?
quiz.why: Desired over have, times volume: 500 / 250 x 5 = 10 mL.

quiz.q: 1,000 mL to infuse over 8 hours. Rate in mL/hr?
quiz.why: Total volume divided by hours: 1,000 / 8 = 125 mL/hr.

quiz.q: Heparin 25,000 units in 250 mL. Order: 1,000 units/hr. Rate?
quiz.why: The bag is 100 units per mL, so 1,000 units/hr runs at 10 mL/hr.
High K gives tall, peaked T waves. U waves point to low K.
Facial twitching when the cheek is tapped means low calcium. Think tetany.
Airborne: N95 respirator and a negative-pressure room.

quiz.q: Hand hygiene after caring for a client with C. diff?
quiz.why: Alcohol doesn't kill C. diff spores. Soap and water remove them.
Glargine is long-acting and peakless. It gives steady basal coverage.
About 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L. Above 1.5, watch for toxicity.

quiz.q: Hold an adult's digoxin if apical pulse is below:
quiz.why: Check the apical pulse for a full minute. Hold if under 60 and notify the provider.

quiz.q: Expected finding in left-sided heart failure?
quiz.why: Left backs up into the lungs. The other three are right-sided signs.

quiz.q: A client on an MAOI should avoid:
quiz.why: Aged cheese is high in tyramine, which can trigger a hypertensive crisis.

myth.myth: The NCLEX shuts off at 85 questions only if you fail.
myth.fact: It stops once it's confident you're above or below passing. That can happen at 85 for either result.

myth.myth: A surgical mask is enough for airborne precautions.
myth.fact: Airborne needs an N95 or PAPR and a negative-pressure room. Think TB, measles and varicella.

myth.myth: IV potassium can be pushed in an emergency.
myth.fact: Never IV push potassium. It's always diluted and run on a pump.
Crackles can come from heart failure, pneumonia or atelectasis. Look at the whole picture.

myth.myth: If vital signs are normal, the pain isn't real.
myth.fact: Pain is what the client says it is. Chronic pain often comes with normal vitals.

myth.myth: Massage a reddened bony area to help circulation.
myth.fact: Don't massage reddened bony areas. It can deepen tissue damage. Reposition and offload instead.

myth.myth: Insulins can be drawn up in any order.
myth.fact: Clear before cloudy: draw up regular before NPH.
Restraints need a time-limited order, never PRN, plus frequent checks.

myth.myth: Elevate the legs for any leg pain.
myth.fact: Elevate for venous problems. For arterial insufficiency, keep the legs dependent.
The RN keeps assessment, teaching, evaluation and unstable clients. UAPs handle ADLs and stable vitals.

myth.myth: Never give oxygen to a client with COPD.
myth.fact: Never withhold oxygen from a hypoxic client. Titrate to the ordered target, often 88 to 92%.

myth.myth: Take nitroglycerin as often as needed for chest pain.
myth.fact: One dose every 5 minutes, up to 3. Call 911 if pain isn't better 5 minutes after the first.

myth.myth: A stable stroke client can have their lunch tray.
myth.fact: Do a swallow screen before any food, fluids or oral meds.

myth.myth: Suction as long as secretions keep coming.
myth.fact: Limit each pass to 10 to 15 seconds and oxygenate before suctioning.

myth.myth: Calling the provider is never the right NCLEX answer.
myth.fact: It's right once you've assessed and the client needs an order or care outside nursing scope.

myth.myth: Fever is always the first sign of sepsis in older adults.
myth.fact: New confusion is often an early sign in older adults. Fever may be absent.

myth.myth: A confused hypoglycemic client should drink juice.
myth.fact: If they can't swallow safely, nothing by mouth. Give IV dextrose or IM glucagon per protocol.

trick.mn: Hyper speeds up, hypo slows down
